newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Ericsson down two pct in wake of H1 result.
newsitem.headline: Ericsson down two pct in wake of H1 result.

text.p: Shares in Swedish telecoms group AB LM Ericsson slid nearly two percent on Tuesday, recoiling from gains after a stronger-than-expected earnings report for the first half of the year published last week.
At 1420 GMT the share was trading at 352 crowns, down seven crowns or 1.9 percent on Monday's close.
PaineWebber wireless analyst Walter Piecyk said the fall could be due to investors digesting the group's second quarter result.
Ericsson posted a 44 percent jump in pre-tax profit for the first half of 1997 and a surprise 100 percent improvement in mobile telephone sales.

"Perhaps investors are recognising that despite Ericsson's strong quarter, revenue growth could slow down based on competitive pressure as well as the fact booking growth was lower than revenue growth for the quarter," Piecyk said.
He said the main concern continued to be Ericsson's mobile telephone business growing as a percentage of total revenue.
"We expect Ericsson to lose market share in every major business segment and we believe this market share loss has already begun," Piecyk said.
Aros Securities telecoms analyst Lars Larsen said the decline was not surprising considering recent strong gains.
"I think the trend has been there in the last couple of days. It could be reasonable to do some profit-taking after the strong surge last week. I wouldn't be too concerned," he said.
